day-77-act-01.title: Retrieval Drill: Run-State and Execution-Limit Vocabulary
day-77-act-01.prerequisites: Day 76 state and retry mechanics; Day 73-75 tool protocols.
day-77-act-01.objective: Recall closed-book definitions of the week's control vocabulary - step budget, retry budget, trace, termination, checkpoint, idempotent effect, disposable workspace - then verify each against code rather than memory vibes.
day-77-act-01.instructions:
1. Closed book: write a one-line definition for each of: max_steps, max_retries, trace, termination, checkpoint, idempotent effect, disposable workspace.
2. Self-mark against the authoritative definitions: project.json controls (max_steps=6, max_retries=2, tool_payload_bytes=4096), the agent.py RunResult fields, and the cli.py TemporaryDirectory workspace.
3. Record which terms were fuzzy; schedule those for tomorrow's recall (spaced retrieval beats re-reading).
4. Distinguish the look-alikes: retry budget (failed observations tolerated) vs step budget (total iterations allowed); checkpoint (persisted state enabling resume) vs trace (the record itself); timeout (one blocking wait) vs deadline (end-to-end bound).
day-77-act-01.exercise_prompt: Score yourself out of 7 on the written definitions before revealing the reference list; log every miss to your retrieval queue.
day-77-act-01.hint: The trace is both the run state and the audit record; a checkpoint is that trace plus counters serialized durably.
day-77-act-01.answer: max_steps: bound on loop iterations (6). max_retries: bound on failed observations tolerated before tool_failure (2). trace: append-only list of {action, observation} pairs. termination: why the run ended (goal_reached|tool_failure|step_budget). checkpoint: durable serialization of trace+counters enabling resume. idempotent effect: repeat application leaves state unchanged. disposable workspace: TemporaryDirectory fixture destroyed after the run.
day-77-act-01.mastery_criterion: Write all seven definitions unaided and self-score honestly before checking the code; 6/7 minimum.

day-77-act-02.title: Failure Taxonomy Drill: Classify Every Injected Fault
day-77-act-02.prerequisites: Day 76 runs of all three fault modes.
day-77-act-02.objective: Sort each observed failure into retryable-corrected, retry-budget-exhausted, or step-budget-exhausted classes, and name the counter that enforced each outcome.
day-77-act-02.instructions:
1. Build the taxonomy table with columns: fault | observation error | counter consumed | status | termination | class.
2. Rows from real runs: invalid_arguments ('../outside.txt' rejected, retries=1, then corrected) -> retryable-corrected; missing_note (not_found three times, retries=3 > 2) -> retry-budget-exhausted tool_failure; loop (six identical list_notes calls, retries=0) -> step-budget exhaustion; oversize write_report (>4096 bytes -> size_limit) -> retryable only after shrinking the payload.
3. Retryable vs permanent: invalid_arguments, not_found, and size_limit are permanent for identical arguments - blind retry is waste; the adapter correcting its next action is what made the retry productive.
4. Map to production: only transient faults (timeouts, 503s) justify blind retry with backoff; permanent faults require correction or dedupe (Stripe's idempotent replay is not failure retry).
day-77-act-02.exercise_prompt: Complete the 4-row taxonomy table, then predict the class and termination for a hypothetical network_timeout fault and justify it with the counters.
day-77-act-02.hint: Ask two questions per fault: would the identical call succeed on retry? Which budget - steps or retries - hits its bound first?
day-77-act-02.answer: invalid_arguments -> retryable-corrected (retries 1/2, completed/goal_reached). missing_note -> permanent for same args, retry-exhausted (retries 3>2, failed/tool_failure). loop -> no progress, step-exhausted (steps 6, retries 0, budget_exhausted/step_budget). size_limit -> permanent for that payload, retryable only after shrinking content. network_timeout -> transient: blind retry justified, bounded by max_retries.
day-77-act-02.mastery_criterion: Given only a fault description, predict the terminal state and which budget is consumed - then verify against a live run.

day-77-act-03.title: Blameless Post-Mortem: The Stuck-Loop Run
day-77-act-03.objective: Write a blameless post-mortem for the loop-fault run: a timeline reconstructed from the trace, exact budget arithmetic, the contributing cause, and checkable prevention action items.
day-77-act-03.instructions:
1. Structure it like an SRE postmortem: Summary, Impact, Root cause, Timeline (one line per trace step), What went well, Action items.
2. Facts only: six identical list_notes actions; zero error observations; retries stayed 0; the run ended budget_exhausted/step_budget at step 6; no report.txt was produced.
3. Contributing cause: the adapter fault='loop' ignores history and re-emits list_notes; run_task has no duplicate-action or progress detector.
4. Action items must be checkable: 'detect k consecutive identical actions and abort' or 'score tool diversity in evaluate()' - not 'make the model smarter'.
5. Stay blameless: the system allowed exactly the bounded waste it was designed to allow - six steps, then safe termination.
day-77-act-03.exercise_prompt: Draft postmortem.md citing trace step indices (e.g., 'steps 1-6: list_notes returned ok with identical files list'). Every claim must cite a trace step or a config constant.
day-77-act-03.hint: Impact = no report produced within the step budget; detection happened via budget exhaustion, not an error observation.
day-77-act-03.answer:
# Post-mortem: summarize-notes loop run
Summary: the adapter re-issued list_notes 6 times; the run terminated at the step budget.
Impact: no report.txt; bounded waste of 6 steps.
Root cause: fault='loop' policy ignores history; no progress detector in the run loop.
Timeline: steps 1-6 identical list_notes (obs ok, files=[alpha.txt,beta.txt]); retries 0; termination step_budget.
Action items: consecutive-identical-action watchdog; progress heuristic in evaluate().
day-77-act-03.mastery_criterion: Deliver a post-mortem where every claim traces to a recorded step or a declared constant - zero speculation.

day-77-act-04.title: Consolidation & Assessment Review: Bounded-Run Evidence Pack
day-77-act-04.objective: Assemble the week's evidence pack - a fresh CLI run artifact, the fault taxonomy table, transition-audit output, and an honest mastery checklist - reproducible by a reviewer from a clean directory.
day-77-act-04.instructions:
1. Regenerate everything: rerun the CLI evaluate into a fresh temp directory; re-run the three fault adapters; re-execute your transition audit.
2. Assemble evidence_pack.json: {run_report, taxonomy_table, audit_rows, checklist}.
3. Checklist items (mark met/not-met honestly): name the three terminal states; replay a checkpointed prefix; classify each fault; explain the idempotent write; bound the retry policy; state the kill boundary honestly.
4. A claim with no reproducible artifact stays marked not-met - that is honest review, not failure.
day-77-act-04.exercise_prompt: Produce evidence_pack.json plus a README command list that lets a reviewer regenerate every artifact in under two minutes.
day-77-act-04.hint: python -m projects.agent_learning.cli evaluate --fixture summarize-notes --output evidence_run.json is the anchor artifact.
day-77-act-04.mastery_criterion: A reviewer can re-run your listed commands and reproduce every claim; nothing is asserted from memory.
